definition: The mains wire (also called the line wire) that carries the high alternating p.d. of the supply, about 230 V in many countries; the fuse and the switch are connected in it.
The mains wire that completes the circuit back to the supply; it stays close to 0 V.
A low-resistance safety wire that joins the metal casing of an appliance to the ground; it carries a current only if a fault makes the casing live.
An automatic switch (a circuit breaker) that opens and cuts off the current when the current goes above its setting; it can be reset once the fault is fixed.
A design in which the outer casing of an appliance is made of a non-conducting material, so the casing cannot become live; the appliance needs no earth wire but still has a fuse.
